full_judgment: 2. The main question involved in these Rules is whether the trial of the Sessions Case should be stopped and the accused released in view of section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure. We omit the facts of the case as they are not necessary; The pertinent facts are that the learned Sessions Judge received the Sessions case for trial on 26.2.90 and by an order of the same date fixed 4.3.90 for framing charge against the accused, 10 of whom were absconding and to be tried in absentia, After certain adjournments charges were eventually framed on 4.9.90. After framing the charge on 4.9.90 the Sessions Case was set down for trial on 7.10.90 and accordingly summonses were issued upon the prosecution witnesses. Upon a prayer from the State that day the next trial date was fixed on 6.11.90. Upon subsequent prayers from the prosecution and also from defence numerous adjournments for trial were granted by the court till 10.7.91 when the prosecution filed hajira of 4 witnesses and the court gave State defence on behalf of the accused being in absentia. That day the petitioners submitted an application to the learned Sessions Judge for stopping the trial and releasing them on the ground of expiry of specified time of trial whereupon the learned Sessions Judge passed an order directing the bench clerk to count the working days and submit the account on 23.7.91. On 24.7.91 the learned Sessions Judge passed an order to the effect that the account submitted by the bench clerk in respect of the time limit of the trial was examined and that it was found that the time limit had not expired till that date. Accordingly he passed order fixing 13.8.91 for trial issuing witness warrant through Superintendent of Police. On 13.8.91 prosecution filed hajira of 3 witnesses. The petitioners made a fresh application on that date under section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure once again intimating the court that specified and extended time for trial in accordance with section 339C of the Code of Criminal Procedure had expired on 25.2.91 and prayed for stopping the trial and releasing the accused. The learned Sessions Judge heard the parties and examined the account of working days submitted by the bench clerk and found that the case was received on 26.2.90 for trial and 339 working days passed on 10.7.91. He, however, held that 164 working days were consumed by time obtained by defence and also by the prosecution for production of the accused who were in jail by the jail authority and this period should be counted towards limitation. The learned Sessions Judge, accordingly, excluded these 164 working days from 339 working days and rejected the application on the ground that 270 working days did not expire till then.
